headline: The admin Users screen can now change roles and delete users, but anyone on the internet can do both without logging in.
what_changed: On the admin Users screen, each person now has a dropdown to set their role: member, manager or admin.
Each person also has a Delete button. It asks for confirmation, then removes the user and all their shifts.
Two new web addresses the app answers were added behind the scenes. One changes a user's role and one deletes a user.

risks.title: Anyone can make themselves admin or delete any user
risks.explanation: The existing "list users" address checks that the caller is a logged-in admin. The two new addresses skip that check entirely. The login guard on the admin pages covers only the screens, not these addresses. So anyone who knows a user's ID can promote any account to admin or delete accounts, with no login at all. Ask the developer to add the same admin check the list uses before shipping.

risks.title: Deleting a user permanently wipes all their shifts
risks.explanation: The database is set up so that deleting a user also deletes every shift they worked. There is no undo, and it is not a soft delete (hiding instead of erasing). Combined with the missing login check, an outsider could erase staff and shift history. Even for real admins, one wrong click loses work records that may be needed for payroll or disputes. Consider keeping shift history, or archiving users instead of erasing them.

risks.title: Role can be set to any made-up value
risks.explanation: The screen offers three roles, but the server accepts whatever text it is sent. Someone could save a role like "superadmin" or a blank value. That could lock a person out or confuse later permission checks. The server should only accept member, manager or admin.

risks.title: Failures are silent on the admin screen
risks.explanation: If a role change or delete fails, the screen shows no error. The admin may think it worked when it did not. The list does reload afterwards, so the true state does show up, but there is no message explaining why.

questions_for_developer: The new change-role and delete-user addresses don't check that the caller is a logged-in admin, unlike the existing user list. Can you add the same admin check to both before we ship?
Can the server reject any role other than member, manager or admin?
Should deleting a user really erase all of their shift history? Or should we archive the user and keep the shifts for payroll and records?
What stops an admin from accidentally removing their own admin role or deleting themselves, so that no admin is left?
good_news: The change is small and easy to fix. The admin check already exists in the code and just needs to be reused here.
The Delete button asks for confirmation before removing anyone.
